releases.notes:
## Highlights

- Fixed persistent serverwide and per-player backpack saves failing with `SyncFailedException` after compressed NBT output closed the file descriptor before synchronization.
- Backpack saves now keep the underlying file stream open through synchronization, preserving atomic replacement and crash-safety guarantees.
- Refreshed the Modrinth project overview and updated the project icon.

## Reliability and verification

- Real filesystem synchronization failures remain visible instead of being suppressed by a compatibility fallback.
- The complete release build passes all 100 automated tests.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/F1nal04/essentials/compare/v3.2.2...v3.2.3

releases.notes:
## Highlights

- Added permanent player-account bans with `/ban <player> permanent <reason>`; `perm` is supported as a shorter duration keyword.
- Added permanent IP bans with `/ban-ip <address-or-player> permanent <reason>`, including the combined player-account and IP ban flow when a player is targeted.
- Permanent bans survive server restarts and remain active until revoked with the matching pardon or unban command.
- Moderation audit output identifies permanent bans clearly, while disconnect message placeholders render their duration as `Permanent` and expiration as `Never`.

## Reliability and configuration

- Updated SQLite moderation storage to represent permanent bans without a synthetic expiration date.
- Existing v3.2.1 databases are upgraded transactionally while preserving timed bans, audit history, record IDs, and revocation metadata.
- Timed player and IP bans retain their existing behavior and command syntax.
- Added focused parser, persistence, cache, message, audit, database-upgrade, and restart coverage; all 100 automated tests pass.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/F1nal04/essentials/compare/v3.2.1...v3.2.2

releases.notes:
## Highlights

- Fixed operators being disconnected with `Invalid player data` when Minecraft synchronized the `/ban-ip` command tree.
- `/ban-ip` now uses a vanilla-compatible argument type; IPv4 addresses and player names remain unquoted, while IPv6 addresses must be quoted.
- Added `/pardon <player>` with `/unban` as an alias for revoking active player-account bans, including previously known offline players.
- Added `/pardon-ip <address>` with `/unban-ip` as an alias for revoking active IPv4 and IPv6 bans.

## Reliability and configuration

- Player and IP pardons now update the persisted SQLite moderation record instead of deleting audit history.
- Audit output records when and by whom a ban was revoked using the existing European date format.
- Player pardons leave separate IP bans active, and IP pardons leave separate player-account bans active.
- Added configuration entries and focused tests for player/IP pardon persistence, cache invalidation, audit formatting, and IPv6 normalization.
- Verified command-tree synchronization by promoting a connected test client to operator and confirming it remained connected.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/F1nal04/essentials/compare/v3.2.0...v3.2.1

releases.notes:
## Highlights

- Added timed player bans with `/ban <player> <duration> <reason>`, including support for previously known offline players.
- Added timed IPv4/IPv6 bans with `/ban-ip <address-or-player> <duration> <reason>` and the `/banip` alias. Targeting an online player bans both their account and current address.
- Added always-on kick logging through `/kick <player> <reason>`.
- Added paginated moderation history with `/history` and `/audit`, including filters, offline-player lookup, active-ban status, restrained coloring, and `DD/MM/YYYY` dates.

## Reliability and configuration

- Added SQLite-backed moderation persistence in `config/essentials/essentials.db` for player bans, IP bans, and kick audit records.
- Timed bans survive restarts, expire automatically, and are enforced when players reconnect.
- Replaced the vanilla ban, IP-ban, and kick commands so moderation actions consistently use Essentials storage and messages.
- Moved Essentials configuration into `config/essentials/essentials.yaml` alongside the moderation database.
- Added focused test coverage for moderation persistence, audit formatting, duration parsing, IP normalization, and configuration behavior.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/F1nal04/essentials/compare/v3.1.0...v3.2.0
